summary: Speaker 1 argues better: two sound supporting reasons survive, while Speaker 2 leans on a straw man and an ad hominem.

points.title: S1's Barbara syllogism holds
points.text: All focused work raises output; remote work is focused work; so remote work raises output.

points.title: S2's straw man breaks the attack
points.text: Turning 'remote by default' into 'never meet' misrepresents the thesis, so the attack on n1 fails.

points.title: S2's junior-onboarding objection stands
points.text: The claim that remote onboarding is slower is a genuine weak premise for S1, conceded in the close.
